concept.name: Parabolic SAR
concept.definition: Welles Wilder's stop-and-reverse system (New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems, 1978): a trailing stop plotted as dots below price in uptrends and above price in downtrends, accelerating toward price as the trend extends and flipping sides when price crosses it.
concept.intuition: It behaves like a trailing stop that tightens the longer a trend runs - the acceleration factor pulls the dots toward price, forcing an exit when momentum stalls.
concept.mechanics: SAR_{t+1} = SAR_t + AF x (EP - SAR_t) for uptrends (minus for downtrends), where EP is the trend's extreme point and AF starts at 0.02, stepping up 0.02 on each new extreme to a cap of 0.20. The SAR is clamped so it never enters the prior two bars' range; a price touch flips trend direction.
concept.formula: Rising: SAR_{t+1} = SAR_t + AF x (EP - SAR_t); Falling: SAR_{t+1} = SAR_t - AF x (SAR_t - EP); AF: start 0.02, +0.02 per new EP, max 0.20.
concept.failure_modes: Wilder himself estimated markets trend only about 30% of the time; in ranges SAR whipsaws constantly, and its always-in-the-market design has no neutral state.
concept.misconceptions: SAR is a stop-and-reverse mechanism, not a prediction of reversal - a flip only says price crossed the trailing stop.
concept.example: Prior SAR 48.28, extreme point 49.20, AF 0.14: new SAR = 48.13 + 0.14 x (49.20 - 48.13) = 48.28 (StockCharts' worked example).
